assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Artery
items.clue: A vessel that carries blood away from the heart.

items.label: Epidermis
items.clue: The single outer layer of cells covering a stem or root.

items.label: Cohesion
items.clue: The attraction between water molecules due to hydrogen bonding.

items.label: Lumen
items.clue: The central space of a blood vessel through which the blood flows.

questions.stem: Why is the wall of a capillary only one cell thick?

options.text: It keeps the distance over which substances diffuse between blood and tissue cells very short.
It lets blood pass through the capillary faster, so that more blood reaches the tissue cells.
It leaves room for a lumen wide enough for red blood cells to pass through side by side.
It allows red blood cells to squeeze out through the wall and into the tissues.

questions.explanation: Exchange across the capillary wall is by diffusion, and the rate of diffusion falls steeply as distance increases. A wall of a single endothelial cell keeps that distance to a minimum, so exchange is rapid.

questions.stem: What is the role of the elastic tissue in the wall of an artery?

options.text: It contracts in waves behind the blood to push it along the artery towards the tissues.
It makes the wall stiff and rigid so that the high pressure cannot burst the artery.
It forms flaps that actively open and shut to push blood forwards along the artery.
It stretches during systole and recoils during diastole, maintaining pressure.

questions.explanation: The layers of muscle and elastic tissue allow the artery to withstand and maintain high pressure. Stretching during ventricular contraction stores energy that the recoil returns during relaxation, keeping blood moving and pressure high between beats.

questions.stem: Why can heart rate be determined by feeling the carotid or radial pulse with the fingertips?

options.text: Because blood is pushed past the fingertips in one surge each time the muscular artery wall contracts.
Because the blood flowing through the artery can be felt as it moves past the fingertips.
Because a pressure wave passes along the artery wall each time the left ventricle contracts.
Because these are the places where large veins close to the surface of the skin carry the heartbeat.

questions.stem: Which combination of features adapts a vein for returning blood to the heart at low pressure?

options.text: A thick layer of muscle that contracts rhythmically, and a narrow lumen that keeps the pressure high.
Valves that open and shut actively to push blood along, and a wall of elastic tissue that recoils.
A pulse that travels along the wall and squeezes blood forwards, and a thick wall to resist it.
Valves that prevent backflow, and a flexible wall compressed by surrounding muscle.

questions.stem: A blood clot completely occludes a branch of a coronary artery. What is the direct consequence?

options.text: Blood can no longer pass through the chambers of the heart, so the heart stops beating almost at once.
The region of cardiac muscle supplied by that branch is deprived of oxygen and its cells die.
Fat from the diet keeps building up on the surface of the clot until the artery bursts open.
The muscle in the artery wall contracts to force the clot along, tearing the artery wall.

questions.stem: What generates the force that draws water up the xylem from the roots to the leaves?

options.text: Evaporation of water from leaf cell walls draws water out of the xylem, putting the water column under tension.
Cells in the root pump water into the base of the xylem, pushing the whole column up to the leaves.
The living xylem cells use ATP from respiration to move water molecules upwards against gravity.
Water evaporates from the open ends of the xylem vessels at the leaf surface, sucking the column up.

questions.stem: Why are the walls of xylem vessels thickened with lignin?

options.text: To seal the vessel completely so that no water can escape through the side walls into surrounding cells.
To provide the mitochondria and cytoplasm of the vessel with a surface on which to generate ATP for transport.
To withstand the tension in the water column so that the vessel is not pulled inwards and collapsed.
To hold the plant upright, which is the only function that lignin has anywhere in the xylem.

questions.stem: In a transverse section of a dicotyledonous root, where are the xylem and the phloem found?

options.text: In separate vascular bundles arranged in a ring near the outside of the root, in just the same way as in the stem.
At the centre of the root, with the xylem forming a star shape and groups of phloem between its arms.
At the centre of the root, with phloem forming a star shape and xylem in groups between its arms.
Spread throughout the cortex, which conducts water and sugars across the width of the root.

questions.stem: The pulmonary artery carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. Which statement about this vessel is correct?

options.text: It is an artery because it carries blood away from the heart, whatever the oxygen content.
It carries oxygenated blood, because by definition every artery carries oxygenated blood.
Its wall is thick and rigid so that pressure from the right ventricle cannot burst it.
Its muscular wall contracts to pump the deoxygenated blood along to the lungs.

questions.stem: Which statement describes how excess tissue fluid is drained and what happens to it?

options.text: It enters lymph ducts through gaps in their thin walls, valves prevent backflow, and the lymph is returned to the blood.
It enters lymph ducts, which pump it along with their thick muscular walls to the kidneys, where it is excreted.
It stays in the lymphatic system as lymph, a separate fluid that circulates without rejoining the blood.
It is pushed back into the capillaries by the valves in the lymph ducts, which force fluid towards the blood.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly traces deoxygenated blood from the body through the heart and back to the body?

options.text: Venae cavae, right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary vein, lungs, pulmonary artery, left atrium, left ventricle, aorta
Vena cava, left atrium, left ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, right atrium, right ventricle and aorta
Vena cava, right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left atrium, left ventricle, aorta
Vena cava, right atrium, right ventricle, coronary artery, cardiac muscle, coronary vein, left atrium, left ventricle, aorta

questions.stem: Which feature of a sieve tube element helps sap to flow along the phloem?

options.text: It has lost its nucleus and most of its cytoplasm and organelles, so little inside it obstructs the sap.
It is dead and empty like a xylem vessel, so there is nothing inside the cell to slow the flow of sap.
Its end walls are solid plates that hold the sap under pressure so that it flows faster along the tube.
It contains many mitochondria, whose ATP is used to push the sap along the tube towards the sink.
